fulltext: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，据 The Information 今日报道，微软董事会在 2026 年 10 月向股东提交的代理委托书（Proxy Filing）中，为 CEO 萨提亚 · 纳德拉（Satya Nadella）申请的 2026 财年（2025 年 7 月 1 日～2026 年 6 月 30 日）总薪酬包为 9,060 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 6.06 亿元人民币）。
这一数字略低于 2025 财年的 9,650 万美元（现汇率约合 6.46 亿元人民币），下调了 6.11%。
报道称，尽管微软的云计算（Azure 个人年营收突破 1,000 亿美元）及大部分 AI 业务均达到或超过了董事会的预期目标，但由于 Xbox 游戏业务的营收下滑，拖累了纳德拉的绩效奖金指标。
纳德拉的基本工资依然维持在每年 250 万美元（现汇率约合 1,672.3 万元人民币），其余 95% 以上的收入依然由与公司长期表现挂钩的股票期权与绩效奖金组成。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，美国总统唐纳德 · 特朗普呼吁数据中心建设方与大型 AI 云厂商向所在社区支付收益分红，以此应对能源涨价问题，甚至实现电价下调，让数据中心更容易获得当地社区接纳。他在 Truth Social 发帖警告称，数据中心不仅要像他此前提出的那样自行发电，还必须将多余电力输送给当地社区，可以无偿供给，也可以对外出售。
美国各地社区一直在抗议 AI 数据中心项目，核心原因是这类设施对地方带来巨大影响。小型社区需要承受电价上涨、噪音污染、水资源短缺、空气污染、森林砍伐等一系列问题，这些都是企业数据中心带来的负面影响。
为缓解当地社区的压力，特朗普要求这些大型企业向受影响社区提供回馈，希望以此换取社区接纳数据中心落地。具体落地方式目前尚不明确，结合这篇聚焦电力的帖子来看，分红形式可能是补贴上涨的电费，以此解决直接影响周边大量居民的痛点。特朗普政府此前已经下令这类企业自行发电，其自产的多余电力可进一步降低本地居民电价。近期还通过一项法案，要求数据中心承担电网升级费用，避免这笔开支由地方居民的税收承担。
IT之家注意到，特朗普在帖文中进一步写道：“某些地区原本极不受欢迎的数据中心项目，在达成经济协议后，获得了当地大力支持。”他的目标是推动更多数据中心落地，文末呼吁：达成协议，推进建设！
这笔回馈分红是否足以争取社区的支持还未可知，经济问题只是矛盾的其中一面。项目依然面临诸多难题：巨大的耗水量、生态破坏以及各类污染，这些重大挑战使得 AI 数据中心无论选址在哪里，都很难获得美国民众认可。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，Micron（美光）当地时间昨日举行了 2026 年度技术网络研讨会，对 DRAM、泛 HBM、NAND 与 SSD 进行了展望，本篇关注闪存类别。
美光本次预告了其预计 2027H2 产能爬坡的 G11 NAND 闪存，这家企业似乎跳过了 G10 世代。
G11 NAND 堆叠超过 400 层，应用晶圆对晶圆键合技术，按面积计算的存储密度是现有 276 层 G9 NAND 的 2 倍左右，同时能实现至高 1.5 倍的 I/O 速率，数据传输能耗则可减少 25% 以上。
在 G11 后，美光计划在 NAND 中导入突破性的高迁移率材料，实现超密集的单元架构，强化节能属性。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，特斯拉 2026 年第三季度财报显示，公司已经在弗里蒙特工厂的一条大批量产产线上启动擎天柱（Optimus）人形机器人的生产。不过首席执行官埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）表示，这条产线还需要大约一年甚至更久，才能达到每周 2 万台机器人的目标产能。
特斯拉在 2026 年第三季度业务更新报告中称，弗里蒙特产线下线的这批机器人，是首批达到量产标准的擎天柱，当前生产流程已经可以支撑商业化产品制造。
特斯拉仅用 46 天就拆除了弗里蒙特工厂原来用于生产 Model S 和 Model X 的产线，为擎天柱的生产腾出场地。
就在近期，马斯克承认擎天柱项目仍面临不少难题，包括机械手的技术难点，以及中国稀土磁铁供应方面的限制。
马斯克在周三的财报电话会议中说，特斯拉已经“在弗里蒙特的大批量产线上开启了我所说的早期生产阶段”，并且“这条百万台级产线的绝大部分设备”已经到位。
“我预计我们至少需要一年，或许还要稍久一点，才能实现每周 2 万台的年化产能。”马斯克表示。他提到，大约有一万项细节需要全部调试到位。由于擎天柱属于“颠覆性的全新产品”，产能爬坡的初期阶段进展缓慢且波折不断。
IT之家注意到，马斯克还介绍，特斯拉计划将特斯拉 AI5 芯片集成到擎天柱机器人上，如果一切顺利，相关工作预计在明年 4 月完成。这款芯片的算力远超 AI4，特斯拉针对擎天柱的使用场景缩减了 AI5 的内存配置。
马斯克预计，特斯拉大约能在 2027 年底解决这款机器人剩余的设计、可靠性与使用寿命问题，届时才会对外供应擎天柱。他称，机器人早期的应用场景集中在工业领域，主要用于需要全天候执行的高危、重复性作业。
马斯克表示，在此之前，特斯拉准备发布一段视频，展示擎天柱完成非预先编程设定的任务，相关视频大概还要一两个月才能推出。
“我仍然坚信，擎天柱会成为全球规模最大的产品。”马斯克说道。随着弗里蒙特工厂投产，以及得克萨斯州的第二座擎天柱工厂在建，特斯拉接下来要面对的挑战，是证明自己能够大规模生产稳定可靠的人形机器人。

Private equity giant Blackstone is putting itself at the center of the AI boom, firm veteran Jas Khaira discussed last week on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt.
It is writing checks via various strategies, ranging from offering massive loans to data centers to investing in frontier AI models and applications.

Earlier this year, the firm launched Blackstone N1 (BXN1), a San Francisco-based central hub for its AI initiatives. The group is led by Khaira, who relocated from New York to be at the epicenter of AI.

Unlike earlier tech cycles such as mobile or SaaS, which allowed companies to reach significant scale with moderate capital, the transition to AI requires staggering amounts of investment. That need for capital is precisely why Blackstone, with its $1.3 trillion in assets under management, could play such a critical role in this tech shift.

Khaira emphasized that Blackstone sets itself apart from traditional venture capitalists through its focus on compute financing and its ability to offer flexible capital structures, ranging from debt to equity. And it has been investing aggressively.

“We’re the largest owner of compute outside of the hyperscalers today, whether it’s investments in neo clouds, investments in data centers, and being able to use that compute strategically to support companies,” Khaira said.

For instance, BXN1 played a key role in several compute-related deals, among them Crux AI, a neocloud launched in partnership with Google to commercialize its custom TPUs, to which Blackstone committed $5 billion as an investor. It also backed four-year-old Etched, a chip startup whose rapid development has caught investor attention. Neoclouds are cloud providers that rent out AI GPU infrastructure.
Blackstone pioneered a financing structure that allowed it to lend massive sums to venture-backed cloud neoclouds by analyzing both committed customer contracts and using GPUs pledged as collateral.

Blackstone’s first such deal came in 2023 with CoreWeave, shortly after that neocloud saw demand explode following the launch of ChatGPT. Despite having only “30 million of revenue and minimal profitability” at that time, according to Khaira, CoreWeave approached Blackstone for a $2.3 billion loan.

CoreWeave was borrowing against the considerable value of its large collection of Nvidia GPUs, with Nvidia also an investor. Blackstone also grew more comfortable with the loan because CoreWeave had contracts with blue-chip customers like Microsoft.
That transaction quickly became the financing model for how Blackstone and other credit institutions provided billions in follow-on debt to CoreWeave and rival neoclouds.

“One of the primary things that we’re looking to is the nature of the customer. And if the customer is an investment-grade customer — let’s say it’s Microsoft or let’s say it’s Meta — the risk gets priced relative to that customer,” Khaira said.

Building on its success with CoreWeave, Blackstone struck other neocloud financing deals, including co-leading alongside Coatue a $10 billion credit facility for Australian GPU provider Firmus earlier this year.

Khaira acknowledged that in recent weeks, the large debt burdens accumulated by these companies and other neocloud operators have begun to raise red flags. Coreweave’s debt alone has since ballooned to about $50 billion, causing Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner to note in a recent CNBC interview, “The collateral that CoreWeave is putting up which is really only GPUs is not good enough anymore. They used that in the past to get cheap debt.”

Khaira said that on the credit side, the market jitters stem from a combination of factors. Interest rates ticked up in September, and hotter-than-expected inflation signals that borrowing costs may keep climbing. The flood of AI infrastructure debt offerings isn’t helping either.

“We’re also seeing higher credit spreads,” Khaira said, explaining that lenders are charging higher premiums on top of already higher base interest rates to finance the AI buildout. “The cost of capital to price in debt for a Meta or a Microsoft has widened out,” he added, pointing out that even tech giants with massive balance sheets and solid earnings are paying more to borrow.

Concerns about the rising cost of debt have spilled into the stock market. Shares of CoreWeave dropped over 20% in recent days, while Firmus scrapped its planned IPO on the Australian Securities Exchange at a target valuation of roughly $30 billion.
“Ultimately, the market wasn’t there at that valuation, and so I think as a result, that deal didn’t get done,” Khaira said about Firmus’ cancelled listing.
“The market is thinking what is the right price for neoclouds, what is the right price for these businesses in this moment when interest rates are moving up,” he said.
Despite those pressures on some infrastructure providers, AI companies simply can’t get enough compute to power their models. Their appetite continues to drive data center buildout.

Khaira downplayed worries of doom-mongers that the massive accumulation of AI infrastructure debt could lead to a widespread credit crisis, or worse, crash the economy altogether. “This doesn’t feel like something where you’ve got 2008 banks that are shaky credits,” he said.
Instead, he pointed out that because the vast majority of data centers are built for hyperscalers, the debt financing them is ultimately backed “by the most creditworthy companies in the world.”

Beyond funding data centers, Blackstone is helping companies adopt AI through a $1.5 billion joint venture called “Ode with Anthropic,” formed alongside Anthropic and Hellman & Friedman this year. Ode supplies forward-deployed engineers to help companies adopt AI and integrate it into their operations, starting with Blackstone’s 280 portfolio companies.

When asked if Blackstone-owned companies are seeing tangible gains from AI, Khaira conceded that “there is definitely ROI, but it is uneven.” He described technology adoption as something that could move in a “sawtooth-type pattern,” which, to skeptics, can look like an oversupply of compute before adoption catches up.

私募股权巨头 Blackstone 正将自己置于人工智能热潮的中心，该公司资深人士 Jas Khaira 上周在 TechCrunch Disrupt 的舞台上表示。
它正在通过各种策略开具支票，从向数据中心提供大量贷款到投资前沿人工智能模型和应用程序。
今年早些时候，该公司推出了 Blackstone N1 (BXN1)，这是一个位于旧金山的人工智能计划中心枢纽。该团队由 Khaira 领导，他从纽约搬到了人工智能的中心。
与早期的技术周期（例如移动或 SaaS）不同，这些技术周期允许公司以适度的资本达到相当大的规模，而向人工智能的过渡需要巨额投资。对资本的需求正是管理着 1.3 万亿美元资产的 Blackstone 能够在这一技术转型中发挥如此关键作用的原因。
Khaira 强调，黑石集团通过专注于计算融资以及提供灵活的资本结构（从债务到股权）的能力，将自己与传统风险投资家区分开来。而且它一直在积极投资。
“我们是当今超大规模之外最大的计算所有者，无论是对新云的投资，对数据中心的投资，还是能够战略性地使用计算来支持公司，”海拉说。
例如，BXN1 在几项与计算相关的交易中发挥了关键作用，其中包括 Crux AI，这是与谷歌合作推出的 Neocloud，旨在将其定制 TPU 商业化，黑石集团作为投资者投入了 50 亿美元。它还投资了成立四年的芯片初创公司 Etched，其快速发展引起了投资者的关注。 Neoclouds 是出租 AI GPU 基础设施的云提供商。
Blackstone 开创了一种融资结构，通过分析承诺的客户合同并使用 GPU 质押作为抵押品，可以向风险投资支持的云 Neocloud 提供大量资金。
Blackstone 于 2023 年与 CoreWeave 达成了首笔此类交易，不久之后，随着 ChatGPT 的推出，neocloud 的需求出现爆炸式增长。据 Khaira 称，尽管当时只有“3000 万美元的收入和极低的盈利能力”，CoreWeave 仍向 Blackstone 寻求 23 亿美元的贷款。
CoreWeave 以其大量 Nvidia GPU 的价值为抵押进行借贷，Nvidia 也是投资者。 Blackstone 也对这笔贷款感到更加放心，因为 CoreWeave 与 Microsoft 等蓝筹客户签订了合同。
该交易很快成为 Blackstone 和其他信贷机构向 CoreWeave 和竞争对手 neoclouds 提供数十亿美元后续债务的融资模式。
“我们关注的首要问题之一是客户的性质。如果客户是投资级客户——比如说是微软或 Meta——那么风险就会根据该客户来定价，”海拉说。
在 CoreWeave 取得成功的基础上，Blackstone 达成了其他 Neocloud 融资交易，包括今年早些时候与 Coatue 共同主导为澳大利亚 GPU 提供商 Firmus 提供 100 亿美元的信贷额度。
海拉承认，最近几周，这些公司和其他新云运营商积累的巨额债务负担已经开始发出危险信号。此后，仅 Coreweave 的债务就飙升至约 500 亿美元，Altimeter Capital 创始人 Brad Gerstner 在最近接受 CNBC 采访时指出，“CoreWeave 提供的抵押品实际上只是 GPU，这已经不够好了。他们过去用它来获得廉价债务。”
海拉表示，在信贷方面，市场的紧张情绪源于多种因素。 9 月份利率上升，且通胀高于预期，表明借贷成本可能会继续攀升。大量的人工智能基础设施债务发行也无济于事。
海拉表示：“我们还看到信贷利差上升。”他解释说，贷款机构在已经较高的基本利率基础上收取更高的保费，为人工智能建设提供资金。他补充道：“Meta 或微软的债务定价的资本成本已经扩大。”他指出，即使是拥有庞大资产负债表和稳健盈利的科技巨头，也要支付更多的借款。
对债务成本上升的担忧已经蔓延到股市。最近几天，CoreWeave 的股价下跌了 20% 以上，而 Firmus 则取消了在澳大利亚证券交易所进行 IPO 的计划，目标估值约为 300 亿美元。
“最终，市场并没有达到这个估值，所以我认为结果是，这笔交易没有完成，”海拉在谈到 Firmus 取消上市时说道。
他表示：“市场正在思考新云的正确价格是多少，在利率上升的当下，这些企业的正确价格是多少。”
尽管一些基础设施提供商面临这些压力，但人​​工智能公司根本无法获得足够的计算来支持他们的模型。他们的胃口继续推动数据中心的扩建。
海拉淡化了末日论者的担忧，即人工智能基础设施债务的大量积累可能会导致广泛的信贷危机，或者更糟糕的是，导致经济彻底崩溃。 “这并不像 2008 年银行信用不稳定的情况，”他说。
相反，他指出，由于绝大多数数据中心都是为超大规模企业建造的，因此为其提供债务融资最终得到了“世界上最有信誉的公司”的支持。
除了为数据中心提供资金之外，Blackstone 还通过今年与 Anthropic 和 Hellman & Friedman 共同成立的一家名为“Ode with Anthropic”的 15 亿美元合资企业来帮助企业采用人工智能。 Ode 提供前沿部署的工程师，帮助公司采用人工智能并将其整合到运营中，从 Blackstone 的 280 家投资组合公司开始。
当被问及黑石旗下的公司是否从人工智能中看到了切实的收益时，凯拉承认“投资回报率肯定是有的，但并不均衡。”他将技术采用描述为可能以“锯齿型模式”发展的事物，对于怀疑论者来说，在采用赶上之前，这可能看起来像是计算供应过剩。

cards.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
cards.title_cn: 数据中心可能抹去数十年来空气质量的进步
cards.summary: 【The Verge】A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI. New an…
fulltext: New research out of Texas shows how data centers are driving up pollution.
A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI.

New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand — with gas turbines or renewable energy — will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim.

Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all planned data center projects were to plug into the electricity grid in Texas and be powered by the anticipated grid mix, soot and smog-forming pollutants would skyrocket, according to a new report from the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC). In just five years, it would be enough pollution to wipe out decades of gains in air quality.
“There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did.”

In that scenario, fine particle pollution or soot from the power sector would more than triple, reaching its highest level since 2006. Smog-forming NOx emissions would increase 136 percent, approaching pollution levels from 2004. Planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution would climb 90 percent above what they were in 2025.

That’s not set in stone, of course. HARC modeled different outcomes based on three different projections for data center energy demand. Many proposed data center projects are speculative and could fall by the wayside. And developers can limit the environmental impact of a data center by building solar and wind farms onsite.

NOx emissions could be up to 10 times lower if data centers pair grid power with renewable electricity generated onsite. But if developers decide to build gas engines on site to power their data centers as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to the grid, the opposite could also play out, resulting in the highest pollution levels possible.

Data center capacity is typically measured by how much power they draw, and Texas has become the leading data center market in this measure with 26 gigawatts of existing and under-construction capacity. Texas is also bracing for four times more proposed data center capacity running on power generated onsite than any other state, according to a separate Wood Mackenzie report published in March. And in many cases, developers are turning to less efficient gas turbine technology in order to speed construction — another trend that’s making the data center boom more polluting than it needs to be.

“There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did,” John Hall, HARC CEO, said in a press release. “The transportation sector, the state, and other stakeholders have been working for decades to successfully bring these [emissions] numbers down, and that progress is now at risk.”

fulltext_cn: 德克萨斯州的新研究表明数据中心如何加剧污染。
新数据中心的涌现可能会使德克萨斯州的空气污染回到 2000 年代以来的最高水平，该州已成为生成人工智能背后的物理基础设施的归零地。
新的和拟建的数据中心需要大量的电力。开发商和公用事业公司如何利用燃气轮机或可再生能源来满足这一需求将决定事情会变得多么肮脏。但到目前为止，情况看起来很严峻。
科技公司和数据中心开发商正在设计新的方法来获得足够的电力，包括建立自己的电源。但根据休斯敦高级研究中心 (HARC) 的一份新报告，如果所有计划中的数据中心项目都接入德克萨斯州的电网并由预期的电网组合供电，烟灰和烟雾形成的污染物将会飙升。短短五年内，污染就足以抹去几十年来空气质量的进步。
“我们的子孙很可能会呼吸比我们更肮脏的空气。”
在这种情况下，来自电力部门的细颗粒污染或烟尘将增加两倍以上，达到 2006 年以来的最高水平。形成烟雾的氮氧化物排放量将增加 136%，接近 2004 年的污染水平。全球供热二氧化碳污染将比 2025 年增加 90%。
当然，这并不是一成不变的。 HARC 根据数据中心能源需求的三种不同预测对不同的结果进行了建模。许多拟议的数据中心项目都是投机性的，可能会半途而废。开发商可以通过现场建设太阳能和风电场来限制数据中心对环境的影响。
如果数据中心将电网电源与现场产生的可再生电力结合起来，氮氧化物排放量可能会降低 10 倍。但如果开发商决定在现场建造燃气发动机为其数据中心供电，以避免连接电网的漫长等待时间，那么也可能会出现相反的情况，从而导致最高的污染水平。
数据中心容量通常通过其消耗的电力来衡量，德克萨斯州已成为该指标中领先的数据中心市场，现有和在建容量为 26 吉瓦。根据 Wood Mackenzie 3 月份发布的另一份报告，德克萨斯州预计使用现场发电的数据中心容量将是其他任何州的四倍。在许多情况下，开发商正在转向效率较低的燃气轮机技术，以加快建设速度——这是另一个导致数据中心繁荣造成比其应有的污染更严重的趋势。
HARC 首席执行官约翰·霍尔 (John Hall) 在一份新闻稿中表示：“我们的子孙很可能会呼吸比我们更肮脏的空气。” “交通部门、国家和其他利益相关者几十年来一直在努力成功降低这些[排放]数字，但这一进展现在面临风险。”

cards.title: Walmart is inviting AI agents to shop for you
cards.title_cn: 沃尔玛邀请人工智能代理人为你购物
cards.summary: 【The Verge】Walmart will soon let AI agents shop on its website for you. Next month, the retail giant will allow you to use an AI agent on the site, with systems in place to let you approve and review purchases a…
fulltext: While Amazon shuts out AI agents, Walmart is letting them in.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Walmart will soon let AI agents shop on its website for you. Next month, the retail giant will allow you to use an AI agent on the site, with systems in place to let you approve and review purchases and set spending limits.

The embrace of AI agents stands in stark contrast to Amazon, which blocked Perplexity’s shopping agent and Meta’s Muse AI assistant. But Walmart is opening its doors to AI shoppers — as long as they follow the retailer’s rules. It has outlined a set of terms for agents, saying that “agents must not take actions beyond what the shopper intends” and cannot change a customer’s payment method. Agents also can only access information needed to complete their task. Walmart says it will block agents that don’t follow these terms.

Agents will connect to new “Agent Profiles” within Walmart. By default, Walmart will require approval for all AI agent purchases, but you can also let it shop within a certain budget, such as up to $100. You’ll also be able to review your agent’s purchases separately from your own in Agent Profiles, as well as turn off the agent at any time.

The retailer has built an “Agent Gateway,” currently available in beta, that connects AI agents through the Model Context Protocol, an open standard that allows AI agents to plug into different services on the web. Walmart says this not only enables AI agents to shop without running into hiccups that they might encounter when navigating a browser, but also prevents them from accessing your shopping history and personal information.

“For example, if a customer tends to buy sourdough bread or a particular brand of milk, Walmart will help the agent find those usual items for the customer without sharing the customer’s broader shopping history with the agent,” Walmart says. The company will let users shop with AI agents on Sam’s Club as well.

fulltext_cn: 虽然亚马逊将人工智能代理拒之门外，但沃尔玛却让他们进来。
如果您通过链接购买商品，The Verge 可能会赚取佣金。请参阅我们的道德声明。
沃尔玛很快将允许人工智能代理在其网站上为你购物。下个月，这家零售巨头将允许您在网站上使用人工智能代理，并配备系统让您批准和审查购买并设置支出限额。
AI代理的拥抱与亚马逊形成鲜明对比，亚马逊封锁了Perplexity的购物代理和Meta的Muse AI助手。但沃尔玛正在向人工智能购物者敞开大门——只要他们遵守零售商的规则。它为代理商制定了一套条款，称“代理商不得采取超出购物者意图的行动”，并且不能改变客户的付款方式。代理也只能访问完成其任务所需的信息。沃尔玛表示，它将阻止不遵守这些条款的代理商。
代理商将连接到沃尔玛内新的“代理商档案”。默认情况下，沃尔玛将要求所有 AI 代理购买获得批准，但您也可以让它在一定预算内购物，例如最多 100 美元。您还可以在代理配置文件中单独查看代理的购买行为和您自己的购买行为，并可以随时关闭代理。
该零售商已经构建了一个“代理网关”，目前处于测试阶段，它通过模型上下文协议连接人工智能代理，模型上下文协议是一个开放标准，允许人工智能代理插入网络上的不同服务。沃尔玛表示，这不仅使人工智能代理能够在购物时不会遇到浏览器导航时可能遇到的问题，而且还可以防止他们访问您的购物历史和个人信息。
沃尔玛表示：“例如，如果顾客倾向于购买酵母面包或特定品牌的牛奶，沃尔玛将帮助代理商为顾客找到那些常用的商品，而无需与代理商分享顾客更广泛的购物历史。”该公司还将允许用户在山姆会员店通过人工智能代理购物。

cards.title_cn: Meta 称 Muse 拥有超过 1000 万用户，其中购物是首要活动
cards.summary: 【Meta】Meta Muse users are adopting the app for shopping and personal productivity, the company said during Q3 earnings. The AI app now has over 10M users.

Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming estimates released earlier this week by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.

But it is how people are using it, and how much they’re spending that has caught CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s attention. Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention.
He also shared that over a quarter of Muse’s engaged users who were shopping via the AI agent, had an average purchase size of over $200, which was surprising even to industry insiders.

“Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before,” Zuckerberg said, referring to the financial technology company that connects payment apps to customers’ bank accounts. Muse uses Plaid’s connector to enable agentic shopping.

Beyond shopping, Zuckerberg said other popular uses for Muse include personal productivity tasks, such as connecting the AI agent to users’ email or calendars. The exec stressed that this indicates users trusted Muse’s security setup, which includes a feature called “Muse Secure VM” designed to protect their data and privacy. He also mentioned that the forthcoming “Muse Confidential VM” will prevent even Meta from seeing users’ content.

Now that Muse has achieved “product-market fit,” Zuckerberg said Meta’s focus will shift to scaling the AI agent, increasing revenue, and optimizing its compute costs. Remarkably, the tech company is forecasting that Muse will eventually bring in more revenue per user than its “family of apps” users do today — meaning its users on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. Currently, that figure is around “several hundreds of dollars annually,” Zuckerberg said.

Meta has said it ultimately intends to monetize Muse by keeping it free for most users, but keeping a percentage of the commerce taking place on the platform. Power users who want access to the most advanced AI models or more tokens will also have to pay.
Zuckerberg also noted that Meta believes Muse will be profitable after it scales.

“On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years,” he told bankers and analysts on the Q3 earnings call. “In the near term, Muse is very compute-intensive to run, but we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale.”

Muse will also play a central role in Meta’s smart glasses strategy. Reality Labs, the division responsible for smart glasses, VR, and the metaverse, is still losing billions. However, the division’s losses are expected to improve from $19.1 billion in 2025 to $15 billion this year.

Beyond scaling and supporting its hardware strategy, Zuckerberg teased the company’s plans for something he called the “Muse network.” He described this as taking Muse from a “single-player game” to one where “your Muses can work with your friends’ and your families’ [Muses].”
“And if you want to buy something, it’s not just navigating to that business’s website; it’s talking to their agent,” he added.

Meta 在周三的第三季度财报电话会议上表示，其人工智能应用 Muse 已被超过 1000 万用户采用，证实了市场情报公司 Sensor Tower 本周早些时候发布的估计。
但引起首席执行官马克·扎克伯格注意的是人们如何使用它以及他们花了多少钱。扎克伯格表示，大约 25% 设置 Muse 的人现在每天都使用它，这有助于提高保留率。
他还透露，超过四分之一的 Muse 活跃用户通过人工智能代理购物，平均购买金额超过 200 美元，这甚至让业内人士感到惊讶。
扎克伯格表示：“格莱德告诉我们，他们以前从未在任何其他服务上看到过像连接器那样的活动。”他指的是一家将支付应用程序连接到客户银行账户的金融科技公司。 Muse 使用 Plaid 的连接器来实​​现代理购物。
扎克伯格表示，除了购物之外，Muse 的其他流行用途还包括个人生产力任务，例如将人工智能代理连接到用户的电子邮件或日历。这位高管强调，这表明用户信任 Muse 的安全设置，其中包括一项名为“Muse Secure VM”的功能，旨在保护他们的数据和隐私。他还提到，即将推出的“Muse Confidential VM”甚至将阻止 Meta 查看用户的内容。
既然 Muse 已经实现了“产品与市场的契合”，扎克伯格表示，Meta 的重点将转向扩展人工智能代理、增加收入和优化其计算成本。值得注意的是，这家科技公司预测，Muse 最终将为每位用户带来比其如今的“应用程序系列”用户更多的收入（即 Facebook、Instagram、WhatsApp 和 Messenger 上的用户）。扎克伯格表示，目前这个数字约为“每年数百美元”。
Meta 表示，它最终打算通过向大多数用户免费提供 Muse 来实现货币化，但保留平台上进行的一定比例的商务活动。想要访问最先进的人工智能模型或更多代币的高级用户也必须付费。
扎克伯格还指出，Meta 相信 Muse 在扩大规模后将实现盈利。
“在计算方面，我们正在建设未来几年为超过 10 亿人提供服务的能力，”他在第三季度财报电话会议上对银行家和分析师表示。 “短期内，Muse 的运行需要大量计算，但我们预计明年将其成本效率提高 10 倍以上，这将使其在收入规模扩大后能够盈利。”
Muse 还将在 Meta 的智能眼镜战略中发挥核心作用。 Reality Labs 是负责智能眼镜、VR 和虚拟世界的部门，目前仍在亏损数十亿美元。不过，该部门的亏损预计将从 2025 年的 191 亿美元减少到今年的 150 亿美元。
除了扩展和支持其硬件战略之外，扎克伯格还调侃了该公司的“Muse 网络”计划。他将此描述为将 Muse 从“单人游戏”转变为“你的缪斯可以与你的朋友和家人的[缪斯]一起工作”。
“如果你想买东西，不仅仅是浏览该公司的网站；还需要与他们的经纪人交谈，”他补充道。
